title: Serial Call and Response ASCII
description: Wait for the computer to ask, then answer with two knob readings and a button's state.

source.title: Arduino docs: Serial Call and Response ASCII

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 2 × knob (10 kΩ potentiometer), 1 × pushbutton, 1 × 10 kΩ resistor, and some jumper wires.
Push the knob into the breadboard, each of its three legs in its own column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
steps.goal: Put the knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. One outer leg of the knob → that same row.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg of the knob to GND.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The knob's other outer leg → that same row.
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the knob's middle leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A0 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's middle leg to pin A0.

steps.clip: Push a second knob into the breadboard, each of its three legs in its own column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
steps.goal: Put the second knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one outer leg of the second knob to the blue − row.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg of the second knob to GND.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the second knob's other outer leg to the red + row.
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the second knob's other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the second knob's middle leg to pin A1 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A1 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the second knob's middle leg to pin A1.

steps.clip: Push the button in across the middle gap: two legs above the gap, two below.
hints: The two legs in one column (above and below the gap) are always joined inside the button.
Pressing joins the left column to the right column.
steps.goal: Put the button across the middle gap.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the button's left column (top half) to pin 2 on the Arduino.
hints: Any hole in that column works.
Pin 2 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect one side of the button to pin 2.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the button's right column (bottom half) to the red + row.
hints: When you press, 5V flows through the button to the pin.
steps.goal: Connect the other side of the button to 5V.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the button's left column (bottom half), the other leg in an empty column.
hints: This is a pull-down: it keeps the pin LOW until you press.
Without it the pin 'floats' and reads random values.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor on the button's pin 2 side.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the 10 kΩ resistor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Now the pin reads LOW, and HIGH only while you press.
steps.goal: Connect the 10 kΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. The Arduino says hello until the computer answers. Type any letter in the Serial Monitor and it replies with the two knobs and the button.
